subject.title: trusted-proxy auth: support fallback/default user when identity header is absent

question: Should trusted-proxy mode accept an explicitly configured fallback identity when a request comes from a configured trusted proxy but lacks the configured identity header?
rationale: The requested option would deliberately change fail-closed proxy identity semantics and could authenticate a request that carries no user identity, which automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve a narrow fallback identity
options.body: Add an explicit fallback/default identity option with strict trusted proxy source checks, allowlist interaction, security audit guidance, docs, and regression tests for missing-header proxy requests.

options.title: Reject fallback identity
options.body: Keep trusted-proxy identity header presence mandatory and document Cloudflare IP-whitelist/no-identity WebSocket paths as unsupported unless the proxy forwards identity reliably or the deployment uses the local password path where appropriate.

options.title: Require a stronger proxy assertion first
options.body: Allow fallback identity only when an additional proxy-owned required header or signed assertion proves the request passed the edge policy even though the user identity header is absent.

recommendation.title: Reject fallback identity
recommendation.body: Keep trusted-proxy identity header presence mandatory and document Cloudflare IP-whitelist/no-identity WebSocket paths as unsupported unless the proxy forwards identity reliably or the deployment uses the local password path where appropriate.
